# Proration Edge Cases

Odd situations in which the usual day-based proration rule gives answers that customers question.

## Changes on the billing day

A plan change made on the billing day itself is treated as a change made on the day before, so the customer is charged the new plan for the whole new period and receives no credit for the old one. This is the single most common support question about proration.

## Leap days

Proration divides by the number of days in the period, and a February period containing the leap day has twenty-nine. The system does not special-case it, and the totals can differ by a cent from a hand calculation using twenty-eight days.

## Two changes in one period

When a customer changes plan twice in a period, each change is prorated against the plan in force just before it. The credit lines and charge lines from both changes appear on the next invoice, which can look confusing but sums correctly. The rule of thumb for support is to explain the sum, not the lines.

## Trial conversions

A trial that converts to paid on day ten of a thirty day period is billed for the remaining twenty-one days, including the conversion day, at the paid plan price.
